questions.stem: A host and contractor each assume the other will isolate shared energy sources. What is the strongest preventive control?
options: Let both employers use separate uncoordinated permits
Rely on contract language without field verification
Allow the first crew on scene to decide informally
Define and verify interface responsibilities, isolation authority, communication, and handback before work
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Multi-employer work requires explicit interface control so responsibilities and hazardous states are understood and verified by all parties.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Parallel uncoordinated systems can create conflicting status and gaps.
A contract does not prove the field energy state or shared understanding.
Informal decisions lack controlled authority and traceability.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 4, 31, and 38, multi-employer coordination, management systems, and contractor safety

questions.stem: Vehicle telematics show repeated lane departures near the end of long night shifts. What is the strongest response?
options: Treat fatigue as a system risk and review schedules, rest, workload, supervision, and fitness controls
Discipline each affected driver based only on the telematics alerts without reviewing work schedules
Post general alertness reminders and leave the existing shift duration and workload unchanged
Take no action until a collision confirms that the repeated lane-departure pattern represents a hazard
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Fleet risk management should integrate human performance, work hours, vehicle data, training, maintenance, and reporting.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Individual accountability may matter, but common timing suggests organizational contributors.
A poster is weaker than addressing work design and fatigue exposure.
Near-miss data provide an opportunity to act before a crash.
questions.sourceTitle: NIOSH Work Schedules and Fatigue Resources
questions.sourceLocation: Current ASP11/CSP11 fleet and human-performance objectives; NIOSH work-hours and fatigue guidance

questions.stem: A technician works alone at a remote pumping station with poor cellular coverage. Which protection is strongest?
options: Require the worker to telephone the supervisor only after an incident or equipment failure occurs
Assess the risk, provide reliable monitored contact and escalation, ensure rescue access, and restrict unsafe solo work
Use the worker personal phone as the only control without testing coverage or missed-contact escalation
Allow unrestricted solo work because an experienced technician can recognize and manage every foreseeable hazard
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Lone-work controls should detect missed contact, summon help, and prevent solo performance of tasks whose rescue needs exceed available capability.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Post-incident contact may be impossible when the worker is incapacitated.
Coverage must be verified and backed up for the actual location.
Experience does not eliminate medical, violence, energy, or environmental emergencies.
questions.sourceTitle: NIOSH Emergency Communications and Lone Worker Guidance
questions.sourceLocation: Current ASP11 lone-worker objective and NIOSH emergency communication concepts

questions.stem: An AI tool recommends closing high-risk findings based on incomplete text records. How should it be governed?
options: Allow automatic closure because software is objective
Hide the model limitations from reviewers
Use it as decision support with validated data, human accountability, explainability, monitoring, and override controls
Train the model on prior closure decisions and remove human review
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Emerging technology should be managed through risk assessment, validation, access control, change management, performance monitoring, and accountable human decisions.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Automation can reproduce data gaps, bias, and unsafe historical decisions.
Undisclosed limitations prevent informed use and audit.
Past decisions are not automatically correct, and high-risk closure requires accountable verification.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Current ASP11 emerging-technology objective; Yates Chapters 31, 36, and 38 on systems, measurement, and change management

questions.stem: A storage change increases occupant load and blocks part of an exit access route. What should occur before use of the area?
options: Use the area if employees can squeeze through
Add one exit sign without reviewing the route
Wait for the next fire drill to see whether evacuation works
Review occupancy, egress capacity and continuity, fire protection, accessibility, and applicable code requirements
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Facility changes can affect life-safety assumptions and should be reviewed through controlled design and change processes before occupancy.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Egress must meet applicable capacity, width, continuity, and obstruction requirements.
A sign does not correct inadequate or blocked exit access.
A drill should validate a compliant design, not substitute for review.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Current CSP11 facility life-safety objective; Yates Chapters 12, 29, 35, 38, and 39
